Hi all — attaching the high-level landing zone diagram (network-landing-zone-diagram.png). Key points for Anna / MedTech:

- Connectivity modes supported:
  - Private connector (customer-managed VPC <-> Redwood private endpoint) via VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink / GCP Private Service Connect.
  - IP allowlist over TLS for customers who prefer managed outbound connections.
- Region controls: routing policies can be configured per-customer to limit processing to named EU regions (e.g., eu-central-1, europe-west1). Failover is configurable and defaults to disabled for EU-only tenants.
- Data flow and caching: KV caches and prefix caches are kept in-region; we do not replicate caches to non-EU regions unless explicit failover is enabled.
- Encryption & keys: encryption at rest is enforced using provider KMS; customers can optionally bring keys (BYOK) via supported KMS integrations.
- NAT / egress: For private connectors we recommend setting up controlled egress subnets and NAT gateways; we can provide a sample IP range list for firewall rules.

Limitations / caveats: cross-region synchronous failover is not automatic; it requires a manual toggle or automation triggered by the customer. Observability of requests routed off-region will be logged and surfaced in the Console.

Attachment: [network-landing-zone-diagram.png (PNG)]

—Karthik
